rules: The lookup dataset covers registered properties in England and Wales that have an association to an address containing a UPRN reference.
HM Land Registry records addresses when a property is registered.
If an HMLR address cannot be linked to AddressBase, HMLR creates a new address.
HMLR matches its created addresses and title numbers to new AddressBase addresses when they become available.
Title_No is a mandatory character field and UPRN is a mandatory integer field in the lookup dataset.
Duplicate addresses can exist when supplied information does not match the Land Registry Property Gazetteer.
An address may have a UPRN but no title number when it is not present in the Land Registry Property Gazetteer.
HMLR's first national address database in the 1990s was populated with Royal Mail Postcode Address File addresses.
HMLR moved to the Land Registry Property Gazetteer in 2002 using Ordnance Survey AddressPoint as the national address base.
HMLR adopted Ordnance Survey MasterMap and moved from AddressPoint to AddressLayer2 in 2011.
HMLR moved from AddressLayer2 to AddressBase as its national address source in 2014.
Postal addresses excluded from AddressBase do not have a UPRN and are not available in the lookup dataset.
Where a title number affects many properties, all affecting UPRNs may be associated with that title.
If an AddressBase address has not transferred to LRPG, a title can lack a UPRN even when a UPRN exists externally.
HMLR takes an AddressBase change-only update every six weeks for LRPG matching and title association.
Although data can change several times within six weeks, the published data shows only the last change.
Each registered estate or interest has a unique title number and a title number can have only one class of title.
An application awaiting registration can have an associated title number but no estate-interest or class-of-title information.

The official guide states that a UPRN query is more precise than a coordinate query for registered properties.
Planning Data entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields, together with other fields.
The response geometry and point fields are represented as Well-Known Text.
An absence of API results must not be presented as proof that no planning constraints exist because coverage varies by area.
The guide shows all 337 local planning authorities being fetched in one request using a limit of 500.
A local planning authority entity ID can be reused in subsequent spatial queries.
geometry_entity filters by an existing entity's geometry instead of requiring a raw polygon in the request.
The guide demonstrates brownfield-land filtering within a local planning authority boundary.
A single UPRN query can request multiple heritage and environmental designation datasets.
The location guide combines conservation-area, listed-building, green-belt, flood-risk, Article 4 and tree-preservation datasets.

Each Environment Agency LIDAR ground-truth point is documented with accuracy of plus or minus three centimetres RMSE.
Ground-truth points include attributes such as survey date, surface type and survey method.
A ground-truth survey may support multiple LIDAR surveys when it is less than five years old.
For coastal projects, the ground-truth reuse limit is three years.
The official ground-truth dataset provides a File Geodatabase download.
The official ground-truth dataset provides a GeoJSON download.
The official ground-truth dataset provides a GeoPackage download.
The official ground-truth dataset provides an Esri Shapefile download.
The first-return DSM is produced from the first or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
The first-return DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as the terrain surface.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into approximately 300 survey blocks.
Repeat survey blocks are merged using feathering along overlaps to remove small elevation differences.
An exact TQ2892 metadata feature and survey dates remain unavailable through the current safe transport.
Exact candidate DTM pixel values remain unavailable from the current WCS transport.
OS Terrain 50 contour layers are supplied in GML 3.2.1.
The technical specification recommends understanding XML and XML schemas when processing contour GML.
Each contour tile includes a tile-named GML data file.
Each contour tile includes a metadata XML file with information such as the flying date.
Spot heights are selected automatically as the highest mass point within each closed contour.
A selected spot height is removed when it has the same height as its enclosing contour.
A spot height can be lower than the surrounding contour when a genuine depression exists.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places.
The source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points, breaklines and automated photogrammetric techniques.
The source TIN uses triangles that retain feature edges more accurately than a grid.
